No human clinical study or whole ground Pimenta dioica fruit trial evaluates anxiety severity in Parkinson's disease. Isolated eugenol rodent data conflict between null 14-day oral mouse behavior (Dhara 2020) and paraquat-rat rescue framed around clove eugenol (Uchewa 2025), and culinary pumpkin-spice blend trials (Huang 2022) measured vascular rather than neuropsychological endpoints, so the verdict remains Unknown.

No clinical or experimental study evaluates ground allspice for apathy severity in Parkinson's disease or non-PD human cohorts. Available allspice records cover only multi-spice vascular meal blends, parenteral leaf-extract rat screens, and Caribbean digestive/topical folk uses, so the verdict remains Unknown.

Verdict remains Unknown.

No human clinical study evaluates ground allspice for pain severity in Parkinson's disease. Verdict remains Unknown.

Maybe False (minimal_signal toward easing): controlled human evidence provides no indication that roasted almonds worsen anxiety, and one raw-almond RCT showed lower post-exercise POMS tension (p=0.033) alongside roasted-almond mental-stress HRV improvement (p=0.031), but three null RCTs including a dedicated 12-week anxiety/depression trial (P=0.945) and absence of Parkinson's anxiety data keep certainty minimal.
Unknown (open): no controlled or transferable study establishes whether roasted almond reduces apathy severity in Parkinson's disease.

Unknown (open): five adult RCTs including a 128-person raw whole-almond trial consistently show null effects on attention, while pediatric ADHD syrup trials are active-controlled or bundled with raisins and baseline-imbalanced; no Parkinson's attention trial exists.
Unknown (open): no controlled or transferable study establishes whether raw almond worsens bradykinesia severity in Parkinson's disease.

Maybe False (minimal_signal toward easing): multiple human trials of raw or whole almonds show higher stool frequency (Creedon 2022 Table 5 P=0.034), fewer hard stools (Sartori 2026 P=0.002), and lower hemodialysis constipation (Lambert 2020), supported by oral sweet almond oil RCT relief (Faghihi 2022), opposing the worsening hypothesis while lacking a controlled Parkinson's trial.
Unknown (open): no controlled or transferable study establishes whether roasted almond worsens daily off time in Parkinson's disease.

Unknown (open): two large multi-month whole-almond RCTs found no significant effect on Epworth (p=0.592/0.096) or Karolinska (p=0.892) daytime sleepiness, and no trial has tested roasted almonds or Parkinson's daytime sleepiness.

Unknown (open): three randomized controlled human trials of whole almonds—including a dedicated 12-week trial in adults with depressive/anxiety symptoms (P=0.945)—found no antidepressant effect, and no Parkinson's depression trial exists.
Unknown (open): the only raw-almond polysomnography RCT excluded parasomnias, found null REM sleep architecture differences (p=0.776-0.998), and did not assess dream enactment.

Unknown (open): acute stimulated dental salivary flow (Fitri 2025) and pediatric methylphenidate-plus-almond-raisin syrup adverse-event counts (Mohammadi Kenari 2025) do not establish a transferable roasted-almond effect on Parkinson's drooling severity.

Unknown (open): no controlled or transferable study establishes whether roasted almond worsens dystonia severity in Parkinson's disease.

Unknown (open): no controlled or transferable study establishes whether raw almond reduces fall frequency in Parkinson's disease.

No clinical trial evaluates oral cold-pressed sweet almond oil for general or Parkinson's anxiety severity. Faghihi 2022's oral constipation trial recorded only a bowel-secondary subitem (PAC-QOL constipation-related worry/anxiety (33.5 -> 6.0 vs control 35.9 -> 26.0, baseline imbalanced p = 0.001)) with baseline imbalance, while numerous aromatherapy/massage RCTs used topical sweet almond oil strictly as an external placebo vehicle, so the verdict remains Unknown.

Because the trial lacked Parkinson's patients, lacked a placebo oil comparator, did not confirm cold-pressed extraction, and caused frequent watery stools (53.8% BSFS Type 7), the easing direction remains at minimal_signal (Maybe True).

A double-blind randomized trial of exact ground Pimpinella anisum seed powder (4 g/day x 8 weeks) reduced DASS-21 anxiety in menopausal women versus placebo (30.40 to 4.73 vs 27.93 to 21.73, p < 0.001; Begum/Heyat 2026, n=60), with partial rodent support (Es-Safi 2021; Moradi Vastegani 2023) offset by a null aqueous-extract rat EPM assay (Gamberini 2015) and non-isolatable multi-herb trials. Absence of Parkinson's cohorts and reporting-quality caveats keep the easing lean at minimal_signal (Maybe True).

No clinical study or symptom-matched animal experiment tests ground anise seed for bradykinesia severity in Parkinson's disease. Isolated anethole improved rotenone rat rotarod latency, footprint stride length, and striatal firing/dopamine, but did NOT directly assay bradykinesia severity (no catalepsy/rigidity, tremor, dyskinesia, freezing, or bradykinesia velocity metrics) and tested isolated anethole rather than ground P. anisum seed. Verdict remains Unknown.

Enteric-coated Pimpinella anisum oil capsules significantly reduced constipation severity and defecation difficulty versus placebo and peppermint oil in a double-blind IBS trial (Mosaffa-Jahromi 2016, PMID:27815079, n=120; p < 0.0001), aligning with widespread MENA traditional constipation use. However, the popular Brazilian tea trial (Picon 2010) is confounded by stimulant Senna, ground aniseed powder acted as an antidiarrheal in COVID-19 GI patients (PMC10824915), and no Parkinson's or ground-seed constipation trial exists, capping the easing lean at minimal_signal (Maybe True).

No clinical study or symptom-matched animal experiment tests ground anise seed for daily off time in Parkinson's disease.
